stories.title: Nike launches Vegam Run, its first running shoe designed for India
stories.summary: Nike releases the Vegam Run in India on Sunday, a road running shoe developed for the country in a 55 day product cycle, Retail News Asia reports. It sells first through Flipkart and selected stores, with a full length foam midsole borrowing tooling outlines from the Pegasus 42.

stories.title: Reliance Retail's profit falls 24% as revenue rises 6%
stories.summary: Reliance Retail's net profit fell 24.3 per cent year on year to ₹2,611 crore in the September quarter, as higher costs and a shift in the festive calendar weighed on margins, Mint reports. Revenue from operations rose 5.8 per cent to ₹80,220 crore.

stories.title: Raymond Lifestyle's revenue rises 13.2% to Rs 2,075 crore
stories.summary: Raymond Lifestyle's revenue from operations grew 13.2 per cent to Rs 2,075 crore in the second quarter, led by a 26 per cent rise in garmenting revenue to Rs 339 crore and 20 per cent growth in branded apparel to Rs 559 crore. Garmenting margin widened to 7.4 per cent.

stories.title: Go Fashion's quarterly profit slumps 59%
stories.summary: Go Fashion, the company behind women's bottomwear brand Go Colors, reported a 59 per cent fall in second quarter net profit to Rs 9 crore from Rs 22 crore a year earlier, The Hans India reports. Revenue from operations slipped 3 per cent to Rs 217.6 crore.

stories.title: Ladakh's pashmina brands report new contacts after Lakme Fashion Week
stories.summary: The founders of Changra Ladakh and Norling Looms and Arts met Ladakh's Chief Secretary in Leh to thank the administration for supporting their showing at Lakme Fashion Week in New Delhi. They said they connected with around 30 exporters, designers and professionals while showcasing Ladakh's pashmina craft.

stories.title: AAPE by A Bathing Ape opens its first store in India
stories.summary: Streetwear brand AAPE BY A BATHING APE has opened its first standalone store in India at Ambience Mall, Vasant Kunj, New Delhi, in partnership with Unit Nine, ET Retail reports. It plans to expand into other major cities over the next three years, starting with its Fall/Winter 2026 collection.

stories.title: Victoria's Secret opens its first Ahmedabad store
stories.summary: Victoria's Secret has opened its first store in Ahmedabad, a 3,440 sq ft outlet at Nexus Ahmedabad One Mall run by Apparel Group, Indian Retailer reports. It stocks lingerie, sleepwear, loungewear, fine fragrances and beauty products, with the Very Sexy collection taking centre stage.

stories.title: Hunkemöller opens a store in Jaipur
stories.summary: European lingerie brand Hunkemöller has opened a new store at Pacific Mall, Jaipur, bringing its lingerie, intimate apparel and lifestyle products to the city, IFAB Media reports. Reliance Brands Limited runs the brand in India, and Jaipur is its latest stop.

stories.title: Richa Khemka explains her Vesper collection
stories.summary: Designer Richa Khemka showed her collection Vesper at the recently concluded Lakme Fashion Week x FDCI, under the theme The Unseen. She tells Indulge Express it is about everything that exists beyond what we immediately see, explored through shapes, silhouettes and textures that reveal themselves slowly.

stories.title: Anurag Gupta's collection works with women artisans of Bisokhar
stories.summary: Anurag Gupta's collection at Lakme Fashion Week x FDCI was made in collaboration with the Earthomadic Foundation as a tribute to the women of Bisokhar in Uttar Pradesh. It combines traditional craftsmanship and natural fibres with contemporary design to create livelihood opportunities for rural women artisans.

stories.title: Mini Sondhi turns a letter to her father into a collection
stories.summary: Mini Sondhi's Lakme Fashion Week x FDCI collection, A Letter to My Dad, explores love, vulnerability and the conversations that often go unsaid between parents and children, Indulge Express reports. She calls it her most personal work yet, built from trying to understand her father's experience.

stories.title: Weavers Village styles Miss Kerala 2026
stories.summary: Sobha Viswanath's Weavers Village was the official styling partner for the 26th edition of Trends Presents Miss Kerala 2026, with Poonoolil Silks also contributing, Local Samosa reports. The styling drew on Kerala's textile heritage and handloom craft, around a theme celebrating womanhood and individuality.

stories.title: Indian Embassy in Abu Dhabi hosts a saree showcase
stories.summary: The Embassy of India in Abu Dhabi held Six Yards of India, The Saree Story, with the General Women's Union and a diplomatic spouses' group. It featured a talk on the saree's history and a session by designer Kaushik Velendra on Indian fashion reimagined, DD News reports.

stories.title: Hertunba imagines a world where women dress freely
stories.summary: Florentina Agu, founder of Nigerian label Hertunba, built her spring 2027 collection around one question, what women would wear at night in a world run by women, Vogue reports. Agu says even with her independence there are things she still cannot wear, and this collection is a step toward that.

stories.title: Heineken brings its Studio concept to Lagos Fashion Week
stories.summary: Heineken is debuting its Heineken Studio concept in Nigeria at Lagos Fashion Week 2026, which runs from 29 to 31 October, as part of a decade long partnership with the event, BusinessDay reports. The programme includes a lounge, a runway showcase and an after event.

stories.title: Gucci opens its new store concept on Avenue Montaigne
stories.summary: Gucci opened a four floor, 1,480 square metre flagship at 56 Avenue Montaigne in Paris on 30 October, the first to carry its new retail concept. The idea comes from The Store Show, its Spring/Summer 2027 collection in Milan, and will roll out gradually across its stores.

stories.title: Chanel opens a boutique in Los Cabos
stories.summary: Chanel has opened a boutique at Ánima Village in Cabo del Sol, Los Cabos, with 170 square metres inside and a 200 square metre terrace facing the Pacific, The Impression reports. It brings together fashion, watches and fine jewellery in a space featuring Mexican craftsmanship.

stories.title: Dries Van Noten names a Moncler executive as president
stories.summary: Adrian Ward-Rees will become president of Dries Van Noten on 1 December, taking over from Axel Keller, who steps down after five years, WWD reports. Ward-Rees joins from Moncler Grenoble, where he has been chief business officer since October 2024.

stories.title: Musinsa readies an IPO at a valuation near 10 trillion won
stories.summary: South Korean fashion platform Musinsa is preparing an initial public offering at an estimated valuation of around 10 trillion won, or $7.49 billion, The Korea Times reports. It began in 2001 as an online sneaker community started by a high school student and now backs many independent Korean brands.

stories.title: Singaporean tailor wins Milano su Misura
stories.summary: Javin Tan, founder of Common Suits, became the first non-Italian to win Milano su Misura, Trofeo Arbiter, beating 24 tailors including Savile Row names with a tropical, sailing inspired suit, The Straits Times reports. He started in 2014 with a $25 a day university canteen booth.

stories.title: A Louis Vuitton merchant will lead Bergdorf Goodman
stories.summary: Lanessa Elrod, a Louis Vuitton merchant, will lead Bergdorf Goodman, Retail Dive reports. It is a return for Elrod, who previously worked at all three Exemplar Luxury Group banners, Bergdorf, Saks Fifth Avenue and Neiman Marcus. The full article sits behind the site's browser check.

stories.title: Fashion Trust Arabia names its 2026 finalists
stories.summary: Fashion Trust Arabia has revealed 21 emerging designer finalists from the region for its 2026 awards, Emirates Woman reports. Each will present a collection to an international jury in Doha on 28 November, and winners will be announced at an evening ceremony.

stories.title: Nanushka closes its stores amid losses and debt
stories.summary: Hungarian fashion brand Nanushka has closed all its stores and reduced its headcount to 20 as it deals with losses and debt, according to a report from The Business of Fashion. The full piece is for subscribers.

stories.title: GRT Jewellers completes its takeover of TBZ
stories.summary: GRT Jewellers (India) has completed the purchase of 74.12 per cent of Tribhovandas Bhimji Zaveri from the Zaveri family sellers, TBZ told the exchanges on 30 October, Kalkine reports. The deal, for 4,94,59,775 shares, transfers full control of the listed jeweller to GRT.

stories.title: IGI's profit rises 43% and it raises guidance
stories.summary: International Gemological Institute's net profit rose 43 per cent year on year to ₹1,858 million in the second quarter, beating estimates, as revenue grew 31 per cent to ₹3,980 million on 26 per cent volume growth. Lab grown diamond volumes grew 37 per cent and jewellery certification 47 per cent.

stories.title: Surat Diamond Bourse is still largely empty three years on
stories.summary: The ₹3,200 crore Surat Diamond Bourse, built to move India's diamond trade from Mumbai to Surat, remains a largely empty shell three years after its inauguration, The Indian Express reports. Barely 300 of its 4,200 trading offices are in use, and it has hosted two major events.

stories.title: China's lab grown diamond makers turn to AI chips
stories.summary: Chinese lab grown diamond producers are moving into AI servers and semiconductor cooling as oversupply pushes down gem prices, Inshorts reports. China makes around half the world's synthetic diamonds. Industrial diamonds carry margins of about 50 per cent against 30 to 40 per cent for gem grade stones.

stories.title: Sotheby's to auction Pauline Karpidas' $10 million jewellery collection
stories.summary: Sotheby's will sell 70 jewels from art collector Pauline Karpidas in a New York evening sale on 8 December, with a combined estimate of about $10 million, WWD reports. Pieces once owned by Andy Warhol are among the highlights, alongside designs by JAR, Suzanne Belperron, Cartier and Boucheron.

stories.title: Oscar Heyman turns its archive into a holiday book
stories.summary: New York jeweller Oscar Heyman has released A Living Archive, a limited edition holiday book featuring 112 one of a kind pieces valued at more than $22 million, Jewellery Business reports. It mixes new designs with original drawings, antique reference books and vintage advertisements from the company archive.

stories.title: Sarah Jessica Parker brings her Astrea London collection to Dubai
stories.summary: Sarah Jessica Parker, global creative director of lab grown diamond brand Astrea London, has unveiled her second collection with the brand in Dubai after its New York debut, Khaleej Times reports. Founder Nathalie Morrison credited Parker's involvement in shaping the designs, which include the Bloom Collection.

stories.title: Bliss Lau's Vantage collection looks to the Hawaiian horizon
stories.summary: Jewellery designer Bliss Lau's Vantage collection centres on blue-green Guatemalan jade, chosen because its shade resembles the Hawaiian horizon where ocean meets sky, National Jeweler reports. Lau pairs the jade with sculptural 18 karat gold and flowing chains across necklaces, earrings, rings and charms.

stories.title: Gabriel & Co. raises $2.3 million for DKMS at its gala
stories.summary: Fine jewellery brand Gabriel & Co. raised $2.3 million at its annual gala for DKMS, the nonprofit that builds stem cell donor registries for blood cancer patients, National Jeweler reports. The brand also introduced new jewels supporting the charity partner.

stories.title: Bengaluru accessories startup Qiroko raises Rs 1.5 crore
stories.summary: Bengaluru fashion accessories startup Qiroko has raised Rs 1.5 crore in a pre-seed round led by ISV Capital, with angel investors joining, Indian Retailer reports. It plans to add watches and bags and expand across its own website, online marketplaces and quick commerce platforms.

stories.title: Blancpain adds Lady B and new Villeret watches in India
stories.summary: Swiss watchmaker Blancpain has introduced its Lady B and new Villeret models, Indian Retailer reports. Lady B is a spherical timepiece marking 70 years of the brand's Ladybird collection. Founded in 1735, Blancpain says it has never produced a quartz watch, a record it clearly intends to keep.

stories.title: Outlook Luxe looks at Diljit Dosanjh's watch collection
stories.summary: Outlook Luxe profiles Diljit Dosanjh's watch collection after his recent concert in Delhi, noting that his style mixes Punjabi heritage with international labels and statement jewellery. The piece says his watch choices follow the same approach as his clothes, with no single school of watchmaking in charge.

stories.title: Norman Foster designs his first watch with Lebond
stories.summary: Architect Norman Foster has designed his first watch with independent brand Lebond, Hypebeast reports. The 38.5mm titanium model has an integrated strap and a 12 hour bezel for dual time tracking, with natural titanium and black DLC editions running an ETA 2892-A2 automatic calibre.

stories.title: Zuhair Murad's first ALDO collaboration launches on 2 November
stories.summary: Lebanese couture house Zuhair Murad has teamed up with ALDO on a 20 piece collection of shoes, bags and accessories that launches on 2 November, Fashion Times reports. It carries pearls, polished hardware, luminous finishes and celestial details, designed with celebrations in mind.

stories.title: New Balance readies the TL900 trail sneaker
stories.summary: New Balance is releasing the TL900, a new sneaker inspired by trail walking, next week, WWD reports. It has a suede upper, rubber toe tip, heel stabiliser and mesh lining, and arrives early in the approach shoe trend. Somewhere, a pavement is about to be treated like a trail.

stories.title: Onitsuka Tiger and Varley sign for Brompton Road stores
stories.summary: Onitsuka Tiger and athleisure brand Varley have signed leases with The Knightsbridge Estate for stores on London's Brompton Road, TheIndustry.fashion reports. Onitsuka Tiger opens 3,996 sq ft at 39-41 Brompton Road in December 2026, and Varley opens 3,965 sq ft at number 77 in spring 2027.

stories.title: US appeals court revives a privacy case against Eyemart Express
stories.summary: The US Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit has revived a lawsuit alleging that eyewear retailer Eyemart Express shared customers' prescription details and eye exam scheduling activity with Meta through a tracking pixel, The Times of India reports. A Texas court had dismissed the case.

stories.title: Heydude wants to sell more in North America without new stores
stories.summary: Heydude returned to growth in the third quarter after weak results last year, thanks largely to wholesale revenue from retail partners, Retail Dive reports. The brand wants to sell more in North America but is unlikely to open new stores. The full article sits behind a browser check.

stories.title: Welspun Living's revenue rises 16.9% and it turns net cash
stories.summary: Welspun Living's revenue rose 16.9 per cent to Rs 2,870 crore in the second quarter, and profit after tax rose 13 fold to Rs 169 crore. It moved to net cash from net debt of Rs 775 crore in March, with home textile exports up 18.3 per cent.

stories.title: Indian fabric exporters must declare flame retardant status from 1 November
stories.summary: India will require exporters of specified cotton, synthetic and knitted fabrics to declare whether they are flame retardant in shipping bills from 1 November, Fibre2Fashion reports. Sri Lanka and Bangladesh are major buyers of the fabric basket. The same day, the textile PLI scheme's fourth round opens.

stories.title: South India's cotton yarn prices hold steady amid a cash crunch
stories.summary: Cotton yarn prices held steady in Tiruppur and Mumbai amid weak demand and worsening payment constraints, Fibre2Fashion reports, while cotton prices in Gujarat fell as spinning mills held back purchases pending clarity on duty free cotton imports. Mills will review prices for next month.

stories.title: Shahi's Anant Ahuja on making textile sustainability work
stories.summary: Anant Ahuja, head of ESGI and sustainability at Shahi Exports, discussed decarbonisation, renewable energy, circularity and worker well-being on Fibre2Fashion's first podcast. He also raised heat stress in garment factories and called for closer collaboration between brands and manufacturers on cleaner technology.

stories.title: Rongmei Naga attire shown at a fashion festival in Russia
stories.summary: Traditional Rongmei Naga attire and Manipur's handloom heritage were showcased at the 31st Admiralty Needle International Fashion, Art and Design Festival in St Petersburg from 19 to 23 October, through Delhi Fashion Week's International Reinvent Northeast Season 9, Nagaland Post reports.

stories.title: Bangladesh's customs crackdown tests its fabric imports
stories.summary: Bangladesh's garment exporters are shipping more apparel, but tougher customs checks at Chattogram, rule shifts and clearance delays are making fabric imports harder to predict, Fibre2Fashion reports, as China's share of those imports grows. Exporters face rising compliance and sourcing risks.

stories.title: Turkiye's apparel exports fall 9.3%
stories.summary: Turkiye's apparel exports fell 9.3 per cent in January to August, Fibre2Fashion reports, while apparel imports rose and textile exports stayed nearly flat. Orta Anadolu is closing Kayseri production facilities. The analysis suggests buyers qualify alternatives in Egypt, Morocco, Pakistan and Bangladesh.

stories.title: US apparel prices rise even as import values fall
stories.summary: US apparel consumer prices rose faster than apparel import prices in the year to September, Fibre2Fashion reports, even as US apparel imports fell by value in January to August. It advises exporters to calculate landed costs by product code and country of origin, including the July Section 301 duties.

stories.title: Kering's Marie-Claire Daveu on India's role in circular luxury
stories.summary: Marie-Claire Daveu, Kering's chief sustainability officer, tells ELLE India that India is becoming an important source of innovation, craftsmanship and circular solutions for luxury. Kering partnered with Reliance Brands at the latest Lakmé Fashion Week in New Delhi, where the conversation took place.

stories.title: Set your clothes free opens 14 drop-off points in South Australia
stories.summary: Set your clothes free, described as Australia's biggest textile recycling event, returns to South Australia on Saturday 31 October with 14 collection points accepting clothing, shoes, towels, bedding and fabric scraps, Glam Adelaide reports. Australians buy an average of 53 clothing items per person each year.

stories.title: Comment: fashion's circular economy needs responsible influence
stories.summary: In a Retail Gazette comment piece, Marcel Le Roux of IOSH and Daniel Hatton, founder of the Commonwealth Fashion Council, argue the debate should move beyond whether fashion is recyclable or durable to whether workers across its lifecycle are protected, as social media turns posts into orders overnight.

stories.title: A Jakarta workshop gives old clothes a second chance
stories.summary: Kompas visits Bersibersi Lemari, a production house in Pulogadung, East Jakarta, where sewing machines rework old garments to extend their lifespan. The report notes closets crammed with rarely worn clothes while textile waste piles grow every day. The workshop is betting on the closets.

stories.title: An Iowa City consignment shop bets on quality over fast fashion
stories.summary: The Second Act consignment shop in Iowa City is focusing on quality over quantity rather than competing with fast fashion on speed, Corridor Business Journal reports. Owner Anita Douglas says its core tenets are sustainability, community and quality, and the aim is keeping clothes out of the dump.

stories.title: Lagos Fashion Week returns for its 15th edition with a sustainability focus
stories.summary: Lagos Fashion Week, described as Africa's largest fashion event, is back for its 15th edition with a commitment to sustainability, showcasing dozens of Nigerian and African designers, Africanews reports. Cameroonian designer Queen Tumenta said African creatives now have the spotlight and a lot to say.

stories.title: Why Indian retail founders are learning how markets work
stories.summary: An Indian Retailer feature says Indian retail entrepreneurs are rehearsing their first stock market moves, as names like Lenskart and Meesho list and a line of D2C brands watches. It argues everyone from founders to store managers holding ESOPs now needs to understand how markets price a business.

stories.title: H&M Australia pays $138,600 over kids' nightwear labels
stories.summary: H&M Australia has paid $138,600 in penalties after the ACCC issued seven infringement notices over children's nightwear without the required fire hazard warning labels, Inside Retail reports. The regulator said H&M supplied 4,473 items of four types of nightwear that did not comply.

stories.title: Levi Strauss faces a class action over tariff refunds
stories.summary: A class action filed on 20 October claims Levi Strauss reserved about $80 million plus interest in tariff refunds for its own use instead of returning the money to consumers who funded the payments, WWD reports. Nike, Lululemon and Costco face similar suits.

stories.title: When does a vintage remake become a rip-off?
stories.summary: Glossy's luxury briefing looks at the debate over Conner Ives' coats and the influence of secondhand fashion on luxury design. Shoppers asking a Seattle vintage store for the Conner Ives look are spending upward of $1,600, the newsletter reports. Originality, it seems, is also available pre-owned.

stories.title: The RealReal hires eBay's fashion chief as merchandising head
stories.summary: The RealReal has appointed Alexis Hoopes as chief merchandising officer, Oui Speak Fashion reports. She joins from eBay, where she led its $10 billion global fashion business and expanded its Authenticity Guarantee programme, and will focus on the luxury assortment and personalised discovery.

stories.title: Drapers rounds up the week's fashion retail people moves
stories.summary: Drapers' weekly round-up of fashion retail moves includes Superdry promoting Matt Brewster to commercial director, Nigel Oddy leaving American Golf, and Skechers appointing former Snipes chief executive Dennis Schröder as managing director for Europe, the Middle East and Africa.

stories.title: Adidas bets on local production in China
stories.summary: Adidas is relying on local production, design and marketing in China, and Greater China revenue grew in the third quarter while Europe fell, Fibre2Fashion reports. Apparel growth helped offset weaker lifestyle footwear demand, excess inventory and discounting.

stories.title: Avery Dennison's quarterly sales rise 5.2% to $2.33 billion
stories.summary: Avery Dennison's third quarter net sales rose 5.2 per cent year on year to $2.33 billion, with organic sales up 3.7 per cent, Fibre2Fashion reports. Net income rose 2 per cent to $169.7 million, and the company expects full year adjusted earnings per share of $10.10 to $10.24.

stories.title: Apranga's retail turnover rises 8.8%
stories.summary: Lithuanian fashion retailer Apranga's third quarter retail turnover rose 8.8 per cent year on year to €108.5 million, led by 10.8 per cent growth in Lithuania, Fibre2Fashion reports. Nine month net profit climbed 28.7 per cent to €15.5 million, and online turnover grew 11.9 per cent.

stories.title: UK fashion sales jump as shoppers buy winter clothes
stories.summary: Like for like sales across UK fashion, lifestyle and homewares rose 4.6 per cent year on year in October, the strongest growth since January 2025, according to BDO's High Street Sales Tracker, Retail Gazette reports. Online sales rose 10.1 per cent against 2.2 per cent in stores.

stories.title: Roots' chief executive exits after its go-private deal
stories.summary: The chief executive of Canadian outdoor retailer Roots has stepped down following its go-private deal, Retail Dive's Weekly Closeout reports, while the FTC has been focusing on how retailers set prices. The full article sits behind the site's browser check.

stories.title: Michael Kors finds Gen Z shoppers on TikTok Shop
stories.summary: Michael Kors' TikTok Shop is running at almost four times initial expectations, Capri chief executive John Idol said on the 30 October earnings call, Glossy reports, finding Gen Z shoppers who almost did not know the brand existed. It comes as the brand cuts promotions.

stories.title: How ChatGPT's try on button works
stories.summary: OpenAI added virtual try on inside ChatGPT on 1 October, letting shoppers ask about a jacket, upload a photo and see roughly how it looks on them, Yahoo Tech explains. The feature used to live inside individual retailer apps. The mirror has moved into the chat window.

stories.title: Fanatics rebuilds its outfit curation tool with OpenAI
stories.summary: Fanatics has revamped its Shop the Look outfit curation tool with OpenAI, and the new version generated 10 per cent higher engagement in a pilot, Retail Dive reports. The full article sits behind the site's browser check, so the summary is all there is for now.

stories.title: Most shoppers are not using AI for product discovery yet
stories.summary: Most consumers are not yet using AI for product discovery, according to new research reported by Retail Dive, which suggests retailers look at the quality of their product metadata to prepare for a predicted upswing in AI usage. The full article sits behind a browser check.

stories.title: Amazon's cost to deliver each order keeps falling
stories.summary: Amazon lowered its cost to serve each order for a fourth straight year despite rising AI spending, WWD reports. Shipping costs rose 11 per cent to $28.3 billion in the third quarter while units sold grew 12 per cent, helped by better inventory placement and package consolidation.

stories.title: Moody's ranks retail among the sectors with the highest cyber risk
stories.summary: Moody's ranked retail among five US sectors with the highest overall cyber risk and five with the highest modelled losses as a share of gross profit, WWD reports. Media is the only other sector in both groups. Large digital footprints, it turns out, are also large targets.

stories.title: Revolve says hackers accessed payment card data
stories.summary: Online fashion retailer Revolve told investors in an SEC filing that attackers gained access to multiple company systems and to payment card numbers and expiry dates, The Record reports. Revolve did not say when the attack occurred.

stories.title: Artiso AI raises over €3 million for a fashion operating system
stories.summary: Barcelona based Artiso AI, which builds an operating system for the fashion industry, raised more than €3 million in pre-seed funding led by Criteria Venture Tech, FinSMEs reports. Ganni founder Nicolaj Reffstrup also took part. The money goes to product development and new customers.

stories.title: Stitching the Future series wraps ahead of Lagos Fashion Week
stories.summary: Stitching the Future, a series on technology, AI, intellectual property and investment in African fashion by Black Girls in Tech Nigeria and TFB STUDIOS with FOLA, ended with a live finale on 27 October, Style Rave reports. Its premise is that protectable assets matter as much as runways.

stories.title: Bershka opens at Westgate Oxford
stories.summary: Bershka opened a store at Landsec's Westgate Oxford shopping centre on 29 October, Retail Gazette reports. It follows recent additions there including Sephora and Lego. Landsec's Pablo Sueiras said the brand reinforces the centre's position as a leading retail and leisure destination.

stories.title: FatFace opens its first Altrincham store
stories.summary: FatFace is opening a 1,550 sq ft store in Altrincham's Stamford Quarter this autumn, its first in the town, creating six jobs, Retail Gazette reports. It will carry core lines and the new winter collection, including a V&A collaboration inspired by the world of Wonderland.

stories.title: lov. offers $3,000 grants to Gujarat artisans
stories.summary: LOV. Foundation and XTANT invite artisans from Gujarat working in textiles, design and craft to create new work on the theme Love Without Ego. Nine selected artisans get a $3,000 grant each and a show in Kutch from 28 January to 1 February 2027. Applications close 20 November 2026.

stories.title: Swarovski Foundation offers €20,000 grants to young creatives
stories.summary: The Swarovski Foundation's Creatives for Our Future Programme 2027, run with the United Nations Office for Partnerships, offers creatives aged 21 to 30 working in art, design, fashion or technology a €20,000 grant, mentorship and masterclasses. The deadline is 9 November 2026.

stories.title: SFWRUNWAY's free sustainability design competition closes 30 November
stories.summary: Students and recent graduates can enter SFWRUNWAY's free Sustainability Design Competition with a four look capsule built mostly from deadstock or existing material. The winner shows the produced collection at its LA Fashion Week in March 2027. Entries close at 23:59 Pacific time on 30 November 2026.

stories.title: iD Dunedin's emerging designer awards take second round entries
stories.summary: Entries are open for the iD International Emerging Designer Awards 2027 in Dunedin, New Zealand, run with Otago Polytechnic, where finalists show at iD Dunedin Fashion Week. Round one has closed, and round two closes on Monday 30 November 2026.

stories.title: Green Fashion Creative Ideas Competition closes 13 November
stories.summary: Vocational students and recent graduates across Europe, up to six months after graduating, can submit a sustainable fashion idea to the free Green Fashion Creative Ideas Competition, part of an Erasmus+ project. Entries close 13 November 2026, with winners named on 7 December.

stories.title: Bloomington Trashion/Refashion Runway takes submissions from 1 November
stories.summary: The 18th Bloomington Trashion/Refashion Runway Show accepts submissions from Sunday 1 November 2026 to Monday 15 February 2027, open to all skill levels, WBIW reports. The show, a fundraiser for the Center for Sustainable Living, takes place at the Buskirk-Chumley Theater on 18 April 2027.

Shopify Operations Specialist for a U.S. Jewelry Brand

Authentication Specialist II - Jewelry and Apparel
Quality Assurance Manager (Toy/ Garment/ Footwear - Remote)
